# Scale verified PCM playback to 64 sources

Base: adapter 0.3.4 `c05bb513e8336bae89dc22c25b26dca41fc281d8`, exact registry engine 0.2.1. App research: `docs/analysis/mixer-all-ready-poc-results.md` and `docs/design/mixer-large-session-architecture.md` at app `cd7782bc7057fc7ed64e8b1d9ef6bd64dae5aa4d` plus retained research artifacts. No copied engine/app source and no legacy engine inspection.

The user explicitly requests Astra xhigh to continue toward scalable 64-track browser playback. Root owns independent browser instrumentation and packed app-consumer qualification. This slice owns the adapter spec, implementation and focused tests. No publication or deployment before review.

## Problem and bounded design

All 64 sources passed complete canonical verification and storage, but two short warm playback/seek trials recorded underruns across all sources. That does not establish a browser track-count limit. Initial and seek readiness currently accept one render quantum (128 frames, about 2.67 ms at 48 kHz), while aligned 4,096-frame storage windows are fetched serially. The pump can also run arbitrarily many refill passes before yielding to queued seek/stop messages. Instrument initial play and seek/resume separately before claiming a measured root cause.

1. Keep every complete source verified and leased before opening playback. Do not change FLAC transport concurrency, hashing authority, storage representation, engine DSP or realtime PCM ring protocol.
2. Keep the existing bounded ring (64 slots) and prepare its full available runway for every source before initial play and after seek. A source shorter than that runway needs its exact remaining tail. Seek must still prove the first fresh full-generation chunk starts exactly at the target, with the context suspended until all sources pass. EOF is valid without fabricated samples.
3. Replace serial window waits with at most four concurrent local Blob reads. Each source has one current and one next canonical window, 8,192 frames by default. Queue descriptors do not allocate PCM. Prefer missing current windows, then prefetch before the current window expires. Ready sources continue to fill while another read waits.
4. Bound each worker drive tick to eight fair passes, yielding to the task queue between ticks. Background reads may complete independently; generation checks discard obsolete results after seek, and close prevents all late publication. Preserve a physical read cap across pending old generations. A stalled read must fail within the existing bounded worker/session lifecycle.
5. Report the complete canonical window allocation bound, including pending reads; do not describe logical bytes as process RSS. Memory remains proportional to source count and configured window size, independent of stem duration. The current full-PCM disk representation is retained.

## Objective gates

Focused tests prove actual concurrent reads never exceed four, one stalled source does not block other ready sources, prefetch overlaps consumption, exact PCM16/PCM24 and short tails, no stale-generation commits, close with outstanding reads, finite tick progress and seek/stop responsiveness. Session tests prove one fresh quantum does not satisfy readiness, every source must have the required runway, EOF and mixed lengths work, and all existing running/paused seek, FIFO, failure, close and clock contracts remain.

Full adapter check and existing packed fresh-consumer gates remain required. Root independently compares published 0.3.4 against the exact candidate archive using sustained 16/32/64-source playback, separately captured initial/seek counters, repeated paused/running/rapid seeks, cancellation, memory bounds and zero new underruns/refused/torn/errors. Include 64 stereo sources through at least one complete minute and repeated discontinuities. Preserve failed trials and source/archive identities. Desktop headless Chromium success does not qualify iPad/Safari or production effects; record those limits explicitly.

Storage write batching and off-thread warm verification remain compatible subsequent slices. They do not remedy playback starvation and must not be silently combined with this isolated diagnosis.

## Status

Spec established and synchronized to GitHub issue 50 before implementation. Independent published-0.3.4 instrumentation localizes the captured failures to playback immediately after seeking: both cold and warm initial eight-second playback intervals stayed clean, while three later seek intervals added 66/66/67 underruns. Retained root evidence: app `e2e/results/mixer-64-playback-baseline-localization.json`. This establishes a post-seek readiness/pump problem in the tested implementation, not a browser track-count limit.

Implemented an all-source contiguous full-generation runway proof, clipping each source to its exact remaining tail. Initial and seek gates inspect up to 32 SDK observation chunks per source per turn until every source has the complete 64-slot runway. They do not accept a count containing stale PCM. The existing suspended-seek/clock/FIFO/close contracts remain.

The pump owns current/next windows with at most four actual reads and one pending read per source. A pending old-generation operation retains physical admission until it settles, then its result is discarded. Ready sources continue during unrelated pending reads. Reads have a 5-second terminal deadline; worker ticks contain at most eight passes and always yield to control messages. At 64 stereo PCM24 sources the canonical window bound is 6 MiB, plus unchanged shared rings and other engine allocations. Custom window requests round down to complete render quanta for actual I/O, conservatively retaining the requested allocation bound.

Full adapter check PASS: **184/184 tests**, format, types, source policy, decoder gate and 158-file package policy. Log `/tmp/miso-64-final-check.log`. The new focused cases cover 64-source head-of-line independence, physical read admission across rapid seeks, next-window overlap, stale-read/close publication, finite ticks, exact PCM24 and irregular window sizes, truncated/rejected reads (including rejection without an Error), mixed short/long initial runways and exact source tails/EOF. Existing transport, verification, cache, deadline and console gates remain green.

Fresh packed Chromium gate PASS: `/tmp/miso-64-final-packed-browser.log`. It asserts all 64 contiguous fresh chunks synchronously at the automatic resume boundary, preserves exact first-output PCM against the independent SDK offline oracle, releases all 64 old shared slots, retains internal backpressure and verifies unchanged suspended clocks. Initial, paused and running seek modes each add zero underruns, refused submissions, torn records and errors; all 11 package assets load and warm opening adds no network/decode work.

Immutable browser-tested experimental archive: `/tmp/miso-adapter-64-reviewed/misofm-engine-web-adapter-0.3.4.tgz`, 153819 bytes, SHA-256 `81f2595d18c7e00ff9af758eff67e9c1cac8061fc2a22aeb587e5a01800f4eb0`. Root's initial immutable candidate (`992ceab50d5868b0261fc980f3b9aa2a440dfc907cc95b789d2785d60e4526b4`) passes two 64-source runs, cold and warm: each has 55 seconds of initial playback plus eight seek/play intervals of two seconds, zero underruns/errors across all sources, eight applied seeks, full 737280000-byte canonical verification and physical HTTP peak four. Retained evidence: app `e2e/results/mixer-64-playback-candidate-bare.json`. That source differs from the final runtime only in normalization of a read rejected without a reason; final docs/types also changed. The bare graph has no production effects.

Root's final-archive app graph adds active EQ and compression per track, all 64 meters and render telemetry. Cold and warm runs each cross natural source EOF with 62 seconds of initial playback and then eight two-second seek/play intervals. Both pass the feed gate with zero underruns/errors; mean render CPU is 21.4%/21.0%. The first cold telemetry window contains one render deadline miss with an 11 ms peak; later cold windows and all warm windows record none (warm peak 1 ms). Preserve this startup event rather than claiming perfect render-deadline qualification. It did not coincide with feed starvation. Retained evidence: app `e2e/results/mixer-64-playback-candidate-app.json`.

Physical iPad/Safari remains unqualified. A pre-existing background pump failure terminates the pump worker, but the open session has no direct terminal-error notification hook; user-visible runtime fault propagation is a separate hardening item, not qualified here.
